issues.title: Why Next.js has had so many security advisories
issues.html:
#​498 — November 20, 2026


Read on the Web



React Status



React Flow 13: Fewer Re-Renders for Big Node-Based UIs — The library behind countless node editors and workflow UIs gets its first major release in two years, with new hooks like useNode that cut unnecessary re-renders in large flows.

Hayleigh Thompson (xyflow)



💡 If you're an existing user, there's a migration guide. Vue Flow has also now joined the xyflow family, alongside Svelte Flow.



How to Build Your Own Automated Debugging Workflow — Factory, Exa, and Bolt connected their coding agents to Sentry so production errors become fix PRs, not tickets. Get the recipes for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or bring your own coding agent.

Sentry sponsor



Why Next.js Has Had 51 Security Advisories This Year — You've surely noticed Next.js is getting a lot of security releases recently, but why? Unsurprisingly, it's AI, which is making old bugs easier to find, with 70% of this year's vulnerabilities found in code at least a year old. The team explains how it's responding and helping us stay up to date.

The Next.js Team



⚠️ In related news, a campaign dubbed React2STEAL is exploiting servers that are still unpatched against React2Shell and the old middleware bypass, in order to publish their secrets. Here's what to check on your apps.



🎬 Remotion Studio is Now a Visual Editor That Writes Back to Code — Remotion lets you make videos programmatically with React code, and this short video shows off how its Studio now works like a timeline editor, where you can drag/trim/keyframe something with the edit written back to your source. Your own components can also join in.

Jonny Burger



📄 When an Import Becomes a Zip Bomb: Catching Bundle Regressions in Next.js – By setting up per-route JavaScript budgets in CI. Sergey Patrakeev

📄 React 19.3's View Transitions, Tested: What Actually Animates? – Hint: not a plain setState. Esteban Trillo

📄 Shared Element Transitions Grow Up in Reanimated 4.8 – Now on by default, and they move the real view. Bartłomiej Błoniarz (Software Mansion)



🛠  Code, Tools & Libraries





React Anatomy: Explode a React Page into 3D Layers — A DevTools extension that splits a running React page into 3D layers mapped to the components that rendered it, with live props for whatever you click. You can try the demo without installing anything.

Nicolas Charpentier



Stepperize 9.0: Type-Safe Multi-Step Flows for React — A popular library for wizards, checkouts and onboarding where you define steps once and get typed navigation, plus guards that block a user from advancing until a step is valid.

Damian Ricobelli



Fate 2.0: The Async React Data Client Now Handles Client State Too — The Relay-inspired data client now manages client-only and offline state through the same views and mutations as server data, and works as a GraphQL client too. It's already replaced Relay and TinyBase in Christoph's game, Athena Crisis.

Christoph Nakazawa



Detent: A Wheel Picker for React with Real Inertia — An iOS-style wheel picker that uses its own physics rather than scroll-snap, meaning that a 'throw' has momentum and lands cleanly on options. The demo on the homepage is very cute and worth… a spin. 😎

Hayder





  • 📊 Recharts 3.11 (above) – Popular charting library. Now with context-based themes and accessible fill patterns.

  • ⚠️ React Router 8.5.2 and 7.18.6 – Upgrade to either version for fixes covering seven security advisories, four rated high.

  • You Might Not Need an Effect 1.2 – ESLint plugin that flags unnecessary useEffect calls. Now 'sees through' popular third-party effect wrappers.

  • ka-table 13.0 – Lightweight React table component. Now a keyboard-accessible ARIA grid and has added fixed columns and virtual scrolling of columns.

  • Redux Toolkit 2.15 – Each store now gets its own RTK Query runtime, fixing long-standing SSR and test isolation problems.

  • 📱 React Native Bottom Sheet 1.0 – Software Mansion's bottom sheet goes stable.



📰 Classifieds



🔥 Let the cloud take the heat. Expo Simulators runs iOS simulators and Android emulators for your agents, and your laptop’s RAM stays free.

⚡ Next.js, Astro or React Router site? Fimo hosts it and runs AI agents that keep it found on Google and in AI answers.

🎬 Your app needs video, not a video team. Upload any format to Hyperserve's API, get back MP4 on a global CDN. Ship video in an afternoon.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • The Next.js team is experimenting with Switchyard, a Go-powered server that sits in front of next start. Currently, it forwards requests to Node, but the plan is to move routing work out of Node and into Switchyard. If you're self-hosting Next.js, this is one for your long-term radar.

  • Solid 2.0 is now stable. Async is now part of the signals graph and server functions have moved into core. There are also new diagnostics aimed at coding agents.

  • If you want to try speeding up your npm package installs, vlt's registry mirror serves much less metadata, making clean installs 20-70% faster and, now, it's open for all to use with no account/token needed.

  • 🐘 PostgreSQL 19 is finally here! If Postgres is part of your stack, our sister newsletter Postgres Weekly covered it in depth this week (please subscribe! 😅)

  • npkill 1.0 (npx npkill) no longer just clears out old node_modules folders, but build output and caches like .next and .turbo too.

issues.title: shadcn's next thing: UI SDK
issues.html:
#​497 — November 13, 2026


Read on the Web



React Status



Declarative Dragging — Rather than designing drag and drop interactions as needed, what if you could declare the possible outcomes and let a library work out the interaction? Dragology is an experimental React library for SVG interfaces that does just that. There are lots of demos to try.

Horowitz, Blinn, and Heer



Debug Errors and Agents Faster: Sentry Changelog Live — A walkthrough of what’s new for debugging errors and performance issues, including fixing production bugs with Seer and tracing the agents you build. Live Q&A. Nov 18, 10am PT. Save your spot.

Sentry sponsor



📊 e18e's Ongoing Benchmarks for JavaScript Meta-Frameworks — e18e is now benchmarking meta-frameworks like Next.js, Nuxt, and Astro on everything from install and build costs to SSR throughput, alongside Core Web Vitals data. Built with input from maintainers, the results can be tracked release by release and have already led to fixes in Nuxt, React, and Solid.

e18e Project



IN BRIEF:

  • ⚠️ Using Vite? A critical flaw allows remote code execution on dev servers exposed to the network with --host or server.host. Update to 8.3.7, 8.2.5, 8.1.7, 7.3.8 or 6.4.6.

  • Storybook 11 beta now has an official post. React projects get faster, more accurate component metadata, and there are type-safe stories and official skills for agents. The final release is due in December.

  • React's docs now explain how to keep field values after an Action, and requestFormReset gets a reference page of its own.



UI SDK: Vercel and shadcn's Headless UI Behaviors Library — A low-level library of behaviors, like keyboard navigation, popups, drag and drop, that you compose into your own components. A core idea is to give a solid base for agents to build full components from. In beta, but you can get started now.

shadcn (Vercel)



How X is Rebuilding Its Web App with React, Relay and Vite — X/Twitter is replacing its decade-old client-rendered React app with a stack built around streaming SSR and Suspense. Lab tests show profiles displaying posts much sooner, and the hydration and chunking fixes make this an interesting case study.

Yagiz Nizipli (X)



📊 Six React Chart Libraries vs Hand-Written SVG – The results are close at native speed but with large gaps under CPU throttling or with large datasets. Pavel Gusev

📊 Remix v3 vs TanStack Start: Fast Pages, Thin Ecosystem – Comparing the same site built in React-free Remix v3 and TanStack Start. Jonathan Arnault (Marmelab)

📱 How Five Web Developers Built an iOS Keyboard Extension with Expo Anirudh Coontoor (Supernova)



🛠  Code, Tools & Libraries





Text.js: React Apps That Render in the DevTools Console — Continuing the trend of rendering React apps everywhere, this new framework heads to DevTools as a host environment, supporting App Router-style routing, Suspense, keyboard input and ASCII fonts. Open the console on the page to see it in action!

Anomaly



Exact: A New Rust-Powered App Framework from Expo's Co-Founder — It isn't React as the UI is written in a small, constrained language called Contract that's designed specifically for agents to write and test, but 𝕏 Andrew Clark says it's "eerily similar" to what he thinks React 20 is shaping up to be.

Charlie Cheever



React Shepherd 8.0: Guided Tours for Apps, Now with a Leaner Engine — The React wrapper (React docs here) for Shepherd, a popular library for building step-based on-page tours. Note that it's AGPL, with a paid license for commercial use.

Ship Shape



  • EmbedPDF 3.0 – Powerful PDF viewer with a drop-in React component and a headless library for adding your own UI. (Demo.)

  • react-virtualized 10.0 – The original list and grid virtualization library, modernized. Now in TypeScript, built on function components, and requires React 18+.

  • 📱 React Native Audio API 1.0 – Software Mansion's Web Audio API for React Native goes stable. Adds spatial audio, and FFmpeg is now opt-in.

  • Mantine 9.8 – Adds an emoji picker package, plus new Diff, PhoneInput and week and quarter picker components.

  • BagUI – A shadcn/ui registry of blocks and templates for SaaS landing pages, like pricing and hero sections.



📰 Classifieds



🔍 Can ChatGPT and Claude read your React site? Run a free SEO and GEO scan with Fimo and see what they miss. By the Strapi team.

🎬 Stop approving mobile PRs nobody ran. An agent tests each one on Expo Simulators and puts the recording in the PR.

Build durable AI agents & workflows in TypeScript with Trigger.dev. If steps fail or code deploys, tasks pick up right where they left off.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem





  • Vectoys is a set of React components that render phones, laptops and other small 3D objects as SVG, with interactive HTML inside their screens. Could be handy for mockups or 'in-situ' teasers on your homepage.

  • 🤖 Chrome's Modern Web Guidance 1.0 is a set of skills that steer coding agents toward modern, Baseline-aware HTML and CSS. The team has also listed the 'top 10 things AI gets wrong' when building for the Web.

  • Need a clip of a component or animation for a PR or README? Paul Irish's chrome-capture tool can record a Chrome tab to an MP4 at 60fps with a single npx command.

  • 📊 The State of JavaScript 2026 survey is now open if you want to get involved.

issues.title: Redux Toolkit's road to 3.0
issues.html:
#​496 — November 6, 2026


Read on the Web



React Status



Discord Dropping Electron and React Native for a Rust Rewrite — Discord, one of React Native's best-known users, is moving away, with its CTO 𝕏 showing off a Rust desktop client built on GPUI using 290MB of RAM, with mobile keeping native UI over Rust code shared with the desktop client.

Tom Warren (The Verge)



▶️ Just prior to this reveal, Software Mansion interviewed Discord's Chas Jhin about how React Native development works at Discord's scale, in the ominously titled 'Maybe React Native Is Impossible'.



Run AI Coding Models on Your Own Machine — Local models are now good enough for everyday coding. Learn to run them on your own Mac or GPU, wire them into your editor and terminal agents, and keep your code private with no per-token bill.

Master.dev sponsor



A Roadmap for Redux Toolkit v2.x and 3.0 — Mark Erikson has laid out the roadmap for Redux (complete with a neat history lesson) with RTK 3.0 expected in six to eight months, going ESM-only with 'React 19-scale' breaking changes. But a run of 2.x releases will ship the groundwork first, starting with 2.14 this week.

Mark Erikson



IN BRIEF:

  • ⚠️ Update to Next.js 16.4.5 or 15.5.29, as appropriate: the November security release fixes seven advisories. Most are Cache Components bugs, so the post is worth reading.

  • 🤖 TanStack Query maintainer Dominik Dorfmeister says work on Query v6 can start once 'slop PRs' stop coming in and taking up his time, leading to a thread on the effects of AI-made contributions on maintainers.

  • Vercel is folding Next.js's Data Cache into Runtime Cache with bigger allocations but… new per-read and per-write pricing. Hobby teams migrate on November 29, but check the dates and prices for your use case.

  • Vercel builds also now block known-malicious npm package versions before and during install, on all plans and with no configuration needed.



Next.js is Prototyping Go(lang) Route Handlers — A merged experimental PR lets an App Router route be a route.go file exporting GET and friends, compiled by Turbopack and run in supervised Go-powered workers. Tim says Rust could follow along the same path.

Tim Neutkens (Vercel)



Understanding React Internals: A Deep Dive — A seven-part, source-grounded tour of React's internals that, unusually, starts from the server end before getting to fibers, lanes and the commit phase.

Alexandre Trotel



Amazon's React Native-Based Vega OS Hits 2.0 — Vega, the React Native-based OS behind newer Fire TV devices, is out of beta. SDK 2.0 takes apps from RN 0.72 to 0.83, bringing the React Compiler and Hermes v1 into play. The release notes go into more detail than the post.

Barak Schlosser (Amazon)



📄 Why We Finally Left Next.js for TanStack Start – Production memory leaks in two Next.js 16.3 releases were the last straw. Harrison Milbradt

📄 Writable Derived State: Stop Synchronizing State – Using clientData ?? serverData instead of a useEffect that wipes user edits on refetch. Corbin Crutchley



🛠  Code, Tools & Libraries





Skullet: Skeleton Loading States Measured from Your Components — Hand it sample data and it renders your real component invisibly, measures everything, and draws a matching skeleton to reduce layout shifts when data arrives. The docs have a neat How it Works section explaining the technique.

Lochie Axon



Parcel 3 Alpha: A Rust Rewrite with React Compiler, Tailwind and RSC — Parcel's core is now a Rust binary with no Node dependency, and the team reports cold builds up to 100x faster than v2. React Compiler (opt-in), Tailwind and MDX are built in, with RSC support in beta.

Devon Govett (Parcel)



🤖 Reticle: Let Coding Agents Verify Their Changes Against Your Running App — A dev-only SDK and MCP server so coding agents can drive your running app, inspect network requests, application state, and console activity, and return a pass, fail or 'can't tell' verdict with what needs fixing.

Reticle Labs





react-resizable-panels Gets a VS Code-Style Workspace Component — Brian Vaughn's popular panel library now does dockable tabs you can drag to split or merge panes, and moved tabs keep their state rather than remounting. There's a live demo here.

Brian Vaughn



  • Preact 11.2 – Now has a runtime for React Compiler output via preact/compat, plus scoped custom element registries in shadow roots.

  • XState 6.0 Beta – "No further breaking changes are planned" for public APIs, and @xstate/react 7 is in beta alongside.

  • TanStack Redact 0.3 – The lightweight, synchronous-only React / React DOM replacement adds browser SPA plugins for Webpack and Rspack.

  • React Native 0.89 RC – Faster text layout and native module calls, legacy bridge APIs gone. Stable expected in December.

  • Storybook 11.0 Beta



📰 Classifieds



🤖 Fimo gives your marketers a visual editor and AI agents for SEO and GEO. No more tickets for your React devs. By the Strapi team.

QVAC allows you to run any AI capabilities for free, on your phone or laptop, privately. Try the QVAC SDK now on GitHub.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • James Long has been reviving Prepack, Facebook's abandoned JavaScript partial evaluator. There's a React demo where a pretend site is server rendered three ways, by React, by Prepack's output (which essentially 'compiles' React away), and a hybrid, with the render times to compare.

  • Node.js 27 Alpha has landed, the first version using Node's new release process (where a release will spend six months in 'alpha' before going Current), while Node 26 is now the new LTS line.

  • Chrome 157 rolled out this week with HTML-in-Canvas now stable. It provides a way to draw real DOM elements into 2D, WebGL and WebGPU canvases. The demos are striking.

  • Vercel has released Geist Serif, a new serif font that shares metrics with Geist Sans so the two can mix cleanly. It's not on Google Fonts yet, but the geist npm package includes it.
